name: Planning Poker
highLevelGoals: The moderator needs to be able to create, manage, and control Planning Poker games to guide the team through the estimation process efficiently and effectively.
The moderator needs to manage their account details, including creation, login, modification, and deletion, to ensure secure and personalized access to the application.
The moderator needs to configure game settings such as estimation scales and participant limits to tailor the Planning Poker experience to their team's preferences and needs.
The estimator needs to be able to join games, view stories, submit estimates, and understand the context of the estimation process to contribute effectively.
The participant needs to see other participants' estimates and have tools like a timer to facilitate discussions and reach consensus during the estimation process.
The developer needs to build and maintain the application according to technical standards, ensuring broad accessibility, performance, and a positive user experience.
The researcher needs access to game data in a non-identifiable format to conduct studies on estimation patterns and team dynamics.
lowLevelGoals: The moderator needs to be able to initiate a new Planning Poker game session by providing a game name.
The moderator needs to be able to add a new story to the current game session by providing a story title and description.
The moderator needs to be able to start an estimation round for a selected story, making it visible to estimators.
The moderator needs to be able to reveal all submitted estimates for the current story to all participants.
The moderator needs to be able to conclude the current Planning Poker game session.
The moderator needs to be able to create a new account by providing a unique username, email, and password.
The moderator needs to be able to log into their account using their registered username/email and password.
The moderator needs to be able to modify their account details, such as username, email, or password.
The moderator needs to be able to permanently delete their account from the system.
The moderator needs to be able to select a predefined estimation scale (e.g., Fibonacci, T-shirt sizes) for the game.
The moderator needs to be able to define the maximum number of participants allowed in a game session.
The moderator needs to be able to choose whether estimates are revealed automatically or manually after each round.
The estimator needs to be able to join an existing game session using a unique game ID or link.
The estimator needs to be able to view the title and description of the story currently being estimated.
The estimator needs to be able to select and submit an estimate from the available scale for the current story.
The estimator needs to be able to access any additional context or notes provided for the current story.
The participant needs to be able to see the estimates submitted by other participants once they are revealed.
The participant (moderator) needs to be able to start a timer to manage discussion time.
The participant (moderator) needs to be able to pause the ongoing discussion timer.
The participant (moderator) needs to be able to reset the discussion timer to its initial value.
The developer needs to implement user interface components for game creation, story management, and estimation submission.
The developer needs to develop RESTful APIs for managing game sessions, stories, estimates, and user accounts.
The developer needs to integrate a database to store game data, user information, and estimation results.
The developer needs to implement a secure authentication and authorization system for user accounts.
The developer needs to ensure the application functions correctly across major web browsers.
The developer needs to optimize database queries, API response times, and frontend rendering for a smooth user experience.
The developer needs to implement a mechanism to export game data (e.g., stories, estimates, participants) in a structured, non-identifiable format.
The developer needs to ensure that all exported game data is anonymized to remove any personally identifiable information.
The researcher needs to be able to request an export of anonymized game data for analysis.
The researcher needs to be able to download the requested anonymized game data in a specified format (e.g., CSV, JSON).
